deck_title: Enterprise Fashion Virtual Try-On: DensePose UV Garment Warp (IDM-VTON / CatVTON) + Face/Hand Lock (c_vton = c_0/(1+u), 1.0000x Lock) vs Naive Generic T2I Overrun

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Enterprise Fashion Virtual Try-On (VTON) pipeline evaluation (warping high-resolution flat-lay garment textures onto 24-part DensePose 3D body surface UV coordinates via IDM-VTON / CatVTON dual-UNet attention while restoring pixel-locked model face, hands, and hair foreground masks so amortized unit cost c_vton(u) = c_0 / (1 + u) reaches 0.5000 at u = 1.0, locking C_active / C_vton = 1.0000x across all 17 pose tiers u in [0.000, 1.000] with 0/17 violated) versus naive generic text-to-image / unwarped inpainting (which scrambles plaid/stripe weave counts, warps embroidered chest logos, and corrupts occluding fingers, inflating retake GPU spend by 1 + u to 1.2500x at T4, 1.5000x at T8, and 2.0000x at T16 across 16/17 tiers) and 64-patch UV warp quadrature.
